prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In frames 1–2, the depth map captures an indoor cafe layout with a standing woman on the far right within arm's reach (~0.5–0.8 m, bright white), a seated man in the center-left (~2.5 m) with a menu within his reach, a seated woman behind and to his right (~3.5–4.0 m, ~1.5 m from him) holding a menu, a pastry case on the far left (~2.0 m), and two tall beverage refrigerators along the back wall (~3.5–4.5 m). In frame 3, as the camera wearer turns left, a foreground counter and red basket (~0.8–1.2 m) and a blurred person on the right (~0.5 m) appear in front of a pastry case (~2.0 m) while a person's arm enters on the far left (~1.2 m). In frames 4–5, a man in a red shirt stands directly in front of the camera wearer and approaches from ~1.2 m to ~0.8 m (putting him within arm's reach in frame 5), positioned between a paper bag on the left (~1.0–1.2 m) and the pastry display case on the right (~1.5–1.8 m). Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground woman in frames 1–2 and the counter in frame 3 from the mid-ground seating and background walls, and tracks the approaching distance of the man in frames 4–5. However, the map is unreliable on transparent glass refrigerator and pastry doors (rendering their interiors as flat planar surfaces), saturates to uniform white on the very close woman in frames 1–2, and blurs object boundaries during the fast pan in frame 3.
descriptions.segmentation: In frames 1–2, the segmentation map outlines the refrigerator on the left-center (merging both units in frame 1 and missing the right unit in frame 2) containing a few small bottle masks, the seated man in front of it (~2.5 m), the seated woman behind him to the right (~3.5–4.0 m) above a partially occluded chair mask, and the close woman partly out of view on the right edge (~0.5–0.8 m). During the rapid leftward turn in frame 3, only two partial person masks in the lower-right foreground (~0.5–0.8 m) are detected, while the counter, red basket, pastry case, and arm on the left are completely missed. In frames 4–5, a large central person mask tracks the man in the red shirt as he moves closer (~1.2 m to ~0.8 m) with his lower body cropped by the bottom frame edge, alongside a small bowl above and a cup below the pastry case on the right (~1.5–1.8 m) in frame 4. The segmentation map provides crisp object-level silhouettes and isolates individual bottles inside the fridge and small tableware near the counter that blend into the cluttered RGB background. However, it is unreliable under motion blur in frame 3, misclassifies the glass pastry display case as a 'tv' in frames 4–5, drops the second refrigerator in frame 2, and fails to segment the paper bag, menus, tables, and left-side display case.
descriptions.pose: In frame 1, the pose map detects the upper-body skeleton and facial keypoints of the seated man (~2.5 m, center-left) facing and looking toward the camera wearer with his right hand raised, alongside the facial keypoints and single arm of the close woman on the right (~0.5–0.8 m) who faces left and slightly toward the camera; in frame 2, both the seated man (now looking down at his menu with both hands lowered within reach of the table) and the close woman look downward, and the woman's skeleton is completely missed while the distant seated woman in the background (~3.5–4.0 m) is never detected. In frame 3, no skeletons are detected at all due to severe motion blur and partial view of the people at the left and right frame edges. In frames 4–5, facial keypoints and a shoulder-and-arm skeleton track the man in the red shirt directly in front of the camera wearer as he approaches from ~1.2 m to ~0.8 m, showing his torso facing forward while his head angles slightly downward toward the counter space between them in frame 5. The pose map makes body orientation, head pitch, and arm geometry explicit—such as the seated man's transition from an upright gesture in frame 1 to leaning over the table in frame 2, and the standing man's downward gaze and lowered arms in frame 5—without visual distraction from clothing or lighting. However, it is unreliable across the sequence because it outputs no magenta hand skeletons in any frame, misses the background woman in frames 1–2 and the foreground woman in frame 2, fails completely in frame 3, and reduces the man's torso in frame 4 to a single horizontal shoulder line due to lower-body cropping.
